# Compound Z for bladder outlet obstruction: a randomized trial

## Methods

Sixty adult men with bladder outlet obstruction were randomized to compound Z 400 mg twice daily or placebo for twelve weeks. Maximum urinary flow rate was measured by uroflowmetry at baseline and at twelve weeks.

## Results

Maximum urinary flow rate increased by 3.1 mL/s in the compound Z group and by 0.4 mL/s in the placebo group, a significant difference in favor of compound Z. Post-void residual volume decreased in the compound Z group. Two participants in the compound Z group reported mild nausea.

## Discussion

The authors conclude that compound Z improves maximum urinary flow rate in adult men with obstruction at standard oral doses, although the trial was small.
